sense: the back part; at the rear

evidence: Cic. Phil. 3.32: ā tergō, ā fronte, ā lateribus tenēbitur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: From the back, behind: the usual way of saying where something is or comes from at the rear. Traupman gives it with the genitive for “in the rear of”.
The rear of a house, a cart or an animal: posterior pars domūs. The adjective posterior answers to “rear” (see back-seat, sēdēs posterior).

terms.gloss: the rear (of a column on the march)
terms.comment: Of an army or any file of people; novissimī are those at the back. To bring up the rear is agmen claudere (Caes. BG 1.25, Lewis & Short s.v. claudō).

phrases.english: Dad brings up the rear; we go on ahead.

sources: Lewis & Short: tergum · Lewis & Short: posterior · Lewis & Short: novus · Lewis & Short: claudo
